# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 9 (Bu-Vb Np9)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Np9
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 9
**Title (English, from literature):** Requesting a fine robe from a combined fund
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin01m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 9* (also titled *Dutiyaupakkhata*) is the ninth training rule in the *Nissaggiya Pācittiya* chapter of the Theravāda *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga*. The rule addresses the situation where two separate lay donors each set aside robe funds to purchase robes for a monk. If the monk approaches them without prior invitation and asks them to combine their funds to buy him a single fine robe, he commits an offense requiring forfeiture (*nissaggiya*) of the acquired robe and confession (*pācittiya*). The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

The rule corresponds to the ninth rule of the *Nissaggiya Pācittiya* division in the *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* and *Bhikkhu Parivāra*, with an equivalent counterpart in the nun's discipline (*Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 19*). It is widely preserved across early Buddhist monastic lineages, having full parallels in the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, Kāśyapīya, and Lokottaravāda Vinayas in Chinese, Tibetan, Sanskrit, and Gāndhārī.
